details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches memcached unchanged as the cache key.

A CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

descriptions.description: CWE-93 Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences

solutions.value:
Upgrade to HTTP::Session 0.43 or later.

Note that HTTP::Session 0.54 includes additional security fixes, but has been marked as deprecated.  Users should migrate to an alternative such as Plack::Middleware::Session.

timeline.value: HTTP::Session version 0.43 released with improved protections against memcached injection
HTTP::Session version 0.54 released, with the distribution marked as deprecated.

The gem declares ext/mkrf_conf.rb as a native extension, which causes RubyGems to execute it during `gem install`. The script performs no native build activity (no mkmf calls, no Rakefile emission, no C/C++ sources are shipped). Instead it collects the installer's hostname, username, current working directory, home directory, and the contents of /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, and /etc/resolv.conf, serializes them as JSON, and transmits them over a TLS TCP socket to geymj1lxqj2u1nzkaqe6zrg33u9yxold.oastify.com:443 (a Burp Collaborator subdomain), with a DNS probe to the same host. The package name mimics the legitimate TDesign Vue component family, but the shipped code is purely an install-time reconnaissance and exfiltration payload.

setup.py overrides the build_py command so that during sdist install it calls hello.fetch(), which downloads hello.bat from raw.githubusercontent.com/misdry01/bookish-octo-lamp/refs/heads/main/hello.bat (a personal GitHub account on the mutable main branch, no pinning, no hash or signature check) and launches it via subprocess.Popen(['cmd.exe','/d','/c', path], creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW), hiding the window. The wheel's bdist_wheel override additionally writes a qap793gl4l_boot.pth file containing 'import qap793gl4l_boot' into the site-packages root, so on every subsequent interpreter start site.py auto-imports qap793gl4l_boot, which re-invokes hello.fetch() and runs the remote batch file the same way. A temp-directory marker gates execution to once per machine but is trivially deletable, making the channel re-armable. vmcheck.py also implements DMI-based VM/sandbox detection, and update() refuses to run inside detected VMs via VMBlockedError, which is analyst-evasion scaffolding consistent with the dropper. The author controls the bytes served from the mutable URL and can change them at any time without republishing the package.

## Source: amazon-inspector (5dcafa44d321e5c6169bbdd949fa1d421e5039bc53d017c00d3e5411f33db5ec)
The sole module shipped in both the sdist and the wheel, main.py, consists entirely of `exec(zlib.decompress(base64.b85decode('...')))` at the top level. The package exposes this module as `py_modules=['main']` and wires it as the `psbool` console_script, so the opaque, compressed-and-encoded blob is decoded and executed unconditionally the first time the module is imported or the CLI is invoked. There is no source, documentation, or API surface — the entire implementation is a single encoded payload, deliberately concealing its behavior from anyone inspecting the package before it runs. A boolean-logic utility has no legitimate reason to ship its implementation as an opaque exec-of-decoded-bytes blob; this is the canonical obfuscated-payload import-time execution shape and causes an arbitrary author-controlled program to run on the installer's machine.

## Source: amazon-inspector (000cea12be23bd792df9085f773c94b79ee13ae70b5154f7d619847bf1b3f0d7)
The package's postinstall script downloads an executable from http://185.212.128.180/chromedriver.bat, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome (or chrome.exe), sets it executable, and later launches it through puppeteer-core. The source is a bare IPv4 address over plain HTTP with no hash, signature, or version pinning, and the URL path is a Windows.bat named 'chromedriver' while the package frames the artifact as a patched Chromium. The same download-and-execute path is also reached from src/browser.js, which calls download() followed by puppeteer.launch({ executablePath }) on first library use, so require()/import of the package will fetch and run the binary even when the postinstall step is skipped via CELEST_SKIP_DOWNLOAD. The destination host is not associated with any legitimate Chromium publisher, and the operator of that host fully controls the bytes that are executed on the installer's machine.

descriptions.value: In FRRouting, bgpd accepts a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) whose outer TLV length does not match the length of the attribute: the mismatch is only logged and the attribute is processed anyway. A BGP neighbor can send UPDATE messages carrying such an attribute that put the reference count of the attribute's interned sub-TLV chain out of balance, so that the chain is freed while routes stored by bgpd (Adj-RIB-In entries and RIB paths) still point to it. When those routes are later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, bgpd reads the freed memory, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. The issue was reproduced with "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured for the neighbor, and the reporter observed that the crash does not occur on every attempt.

descriptions.description: CWE-416 Use After Free: the interned Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLV chain is freed while stored routes still reference it, and encap_unintern() later reads and decrements its reference count

cna.title: frr: bgpd use-after-free of Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs after a malformed attribute length from a peer

workarounds.value: Configure "neighbor <neighbor> path-attribute discard 23" (or "neighbor <neighbor> path-attribute treat-as-withdraw 23") for neighbors that are not expected to send the Tunnel Encapsulation attribute, in particular all eBGP neighbors. bgpd then skips the attribute without parsing it.

Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine.

read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session.

A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.

details: A vulnerability was found in Kingston FURY CTRL RGB Control Software up to 2.0.66.0. The impacted element is an unknown function in the library NTIOLib_X64.sys of the component IOCTL Handler. Performing a manipulation results in exposed ioctl with insufficient access control. The attack is only possible with local access.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'multipart field name (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target CF7 form to have the 'Save every step' option enabled and the Database for Contact Form 7 companion plugin to be active with its 'Expandable' table option enabled, both of which are disabled by default.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the /dbml/svg endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject javascript: hyperlinks by supplying crafted DBML table url, headercolor, or TableGroup color settings. Attackers can send a crafted SVG link that, when opened and the table header clicked, executes attacker JavaScript in the Kroki origin.

The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'buddyforms_form_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when a form configured with the public_submit option is published — a condition met by the plugin's bundled Post Simple template out of the box.

A weakness has been identified in Wuxi Wubang Security Software Wubang Five-in-One Safety Production Management Information System up to 3.5. Affected by this vulnerability is the function DiyFileUpload of the file /ws.asmx. This manipulation causes unrestricted upload. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'fv_player_videos' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the administrator-controlled "Allow visitors to upload videos to their profile" setting to be enabled, without which the vulnerable save routine is inaccessible to Subscriber-level users.

The Lightbox & Modal Popup WordPress Plugin – FooBox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'img alt attribute inside .wp-caption container' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by Subscriber-level users when bbPress is installed, as its bbp_filter_kses filter chain permits img and pre tags while preserving numeric character references inside attribute values, allowing encoded payloads to bypass save-time sanitization and reach the vulnerable sink fully intact. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that bbPress 2.6.20 is installed, a public forum exists, and either the first topic has already been approved or subsequent topics clear moderation. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

A security vulnerability has been detected in sox_ng up to 14.8.1. Affected by this issue is the function read_samples_voc of the file src/voc.c of the component VOC Decoder. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The name of the patch is 0b40408b. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This vulnerability affects the function fs.readFileSync of the file local.provider.ts of the component Custom Page Handler. The manipulation of the argument path leads to path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version test-20261013 is able to resolve this issue. The identifier of the patch is d63aa163f10b6dc1080e2368fe8e71aa95b765cb. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

The environment-modules packages provide dynamic modification of user environment using module files. Each module file contains the information needed to configure the shell for an application.
